---
title: "Writing CANE"
guide-section: "Guides"
description: "Write documents as CANE for few-shot examples, and build prompts."
---

`cane.dumps(doc, variant=...)` writes a document's entities as CANE, typically for the
examples in a few-shot prompt.

- Records come in **reading order**: left to right, outer before nested.
- Anchors have exactly `context` whitespace units on each side (default 1).
- The header is always written, and `NONE` when there are no entities.

## Every record is checked

`dumps` parses each record back as `loads` would. A record that would not land on its own
spans, for example a string that also occurs earlier unannotated, is still written, but it
is reported, so a few-shot example never misleads silently:

```{python}
import warnings
import cane_format as cane

text = "take aspirin daily; then take aspirin daily"
doc = cane.Document(text=text, entities=(cane.Entity(spans=[(30, 37)], label="DRUG"),))

with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
    warnings.simplefilter("always")
    print(cane.dumps(doc, variant="context"))
print(caught[0].message)
print(cane.dumps(doc, variant="context", context=2))
```

| Option | Values |
|---|---|
| `on_mismatch` | `"warn"` (default), `"raise"`, or `"ignore"` (skip the check) |
| `parse_options` | The `ParseOptions` you will parse with, e.g. `match="casefold"` |

## What a variant cannot express

A discontinuous entity in Base or Context, an entity without a label, or a label with spaces
cannot be written. By default `dumps` raises `UnrepresentableError`; `on_unrepresentable`
chooses another strategy, each with a warning:

| `on_unrepresentable` | Effect |
|---|---|
| `"raise"` | Raise `UnrepresentableError` (default). |
| `"skip"` | Leave the entity out. |
| `"first"` | Write only the first span of a discontinuous entity. |
| `"hull"` | Write one span covering all parts and the gaps. |

Relations, concepts, attributes and segments have no place in CANE; `dumps` says so once in
a `LossyConversionWarning` (`lossy="ignore"` silences it).

## Prompts

`build_prompt` writes the examples with `dumps` and the same options, so the prompt teaches
exactly what `loads` expects:

```python
prompt = cane.build_prompt(
    new_text,
    examples=train_docs[:5],
    variant="full",
    labels=["DRUG", "ADR"],
)
```

`cane.guideline(variant)` returns just the guideline paragraph, if you build prompts
yourself.
